'''Kyle Raymond Orton''' (born November 14, 1982) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for [[Purdue University|Purdue]], where he started four straight bowl games. He was selected by the [[Chicago Bears]] in the fourth round of the [[2005 NFL draft]].  After an injury to Bears starter [[Rex Grossman]], Orton was pressed into service as the starting quarterback during his rookie year, starting the first 14 games of the [[2005 Chicago Bears season|2005 season]], but was replaced by Grossman for the playoffs that year.  Orton did not play at all in 2006, and sparingly in 2007. He regained his starting job from Grossman in 2008, but the team finished a disappointing 9–7 and out of the playoffs. In the offseason of that year, he was traded to the [[Denver Broncos]].

Orton spent the next three seasons with Broncos, where he amassed a 12–21 record as a starting quarterback over three seasons. He lost his starting role to [[Tim Tebow]] during the [[2011 Denver Broncos season|2011 season]] and was released by the team. Orton was claimed off waivers by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]]. He spent the next three seasons as a back-up quarterback for the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and [[Buffalo Bills]]. Orton became the Bills' starting quarterback in [[2014 Buffalo Bills season|2014]], where he went 7–5. He retired after the season.

'''Ronald Kyle Clifton''' (born August 23, 1962) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for 13 seasons with the for the [[New York Jets]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). After playing [[college football]] for the [[TCU Horned Frogs football|TCU Horned Frogs]], he was selected by the Jets in the third round of the [[1984 NFL draft]] with the 64th overall pick.<ref>{{cite news |author=Eskenazi, Gerald |title=In His 13th Season, Clifton Knows the Angles |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1996/07/30/sports/pro-football-in-his-13th-season-clifton-knows-the-angles.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=July 30, 1996 |accessdate=October 10, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=1984 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1984/draft.htm |access-date=2023-10-10 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

He led the NFL in solo [[tackle (football move)|tackles]] with 160 in 1985, 174 in 1986 and 162 in 1988. Additionally, he was in the top 10 of NFL solo tacklers in 1984, 1985, 1986, 1988, 1989, 1990, and 1991. He briefly took the lead in career combined tackles away from Clay Matthews in 1993. He announced his retirement on February 14, 1997.<ref>{{cite news |author=Mallozzi, Vincent M. |title=Clifton, a Career Jet, Retires |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1997/02/15/sports/clifton-a-career-jet-retires.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=February 15, 1997 |accessdate=October 10, 2019}}</ref> At the time of his retirement, he was the second-leading tackler in NFL history and remains the Jets' all-time leading tackler. Clifton made 1,484 tackles over the course of his professional career ranking him 10th overall in combined tackles since 1987.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=NFL Tackles Combined Career Leaders (since 1987)|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/leaders/tackles_combined_career.htm|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=November 6, 2020|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> Clifton attended high school in [[Bridgeport, Texas]].

'''Kyle Kramer''' (born January 12, 1967) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played for the [[Cleveland Browns]] in 1989.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KramKy20.htm |title=Kyle Kramer Stats |publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.com |date= |access-date=March 2, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/kylekramer/2518805/profile |title=Kyle Kramer, DB |work=Nfl.com |date= |access-date=March 2, 2020}}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[Bowling Green Falcons football|Bowling Green Falcons]] and was selected by the Browns in the fifth round of the [[1989 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1989 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1989/draft.htm |access-date=May 26, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Kramer was inducted into the 2020 Kettering Fairmont High School Hall of Fame. Earning 6 varsity letter in Football and Track. He was named most Valuable Defensive Back in 1984 and most Valuable in Track in 1984 and 1985. Kramer was the first KFHS graduate to play in the NFL.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2000 Hall of Fame |url=https://sideeffectsproduction.blob.core.windows.net/embed/bddf62296ba54cf992fd81b6e9399af6/walloffame.html#/walloffame/attract |access-date=Aug 28, 2023 |website=KF Firebirds.com |language=en}}</ref>

Kramer was inducted to the Bowling Green Hall of Fame in 2011. He was a four-year letter winner and a three-year starter at safety for the football Falcons. A two-time All-Mid-American Conference First-Team selection and earned All-American honorable his last two seasons. As a senior, Kramer was a team co-captain, and was named the Falcons’ Most Valuable Player. He led the team with a total of 143 tackles, ranking fifth in the MAC. Kramer’s career total of 399 tackles during his college career was the third highest in BGSU history at the time of his graduation, and still ranks today. He was named to the Academic All-MAC Team on two occasions. He Studied Bio Pre-Med.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 Hall of Fame |url=https://bgsufalcons.com/honors/hall-of-fame/kyle-kramer/215 |access-date=Aug 28, 2023 |website=BGSU Falcons.com |language=en}}</ref>

He was selected by the Cleveland Browns in the fifth round of the 1989 NFL draft with the 114th overall pick. During his career, he had 17 special teams stops during the regular season as a rookie in ‘89, and recorded his first NFL interception in the Dec. 17 game vs. Minnesota. He missed several games due to a thigh injury that year. He suffered a career ending injury during the Hall of Fame Game in 1990. Kramer was with the Browns until 1991.

'''Kyle Douglas Morrell''' (October 9, 1963 – November 15, 2020) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

Morrell was born in [[Scottsdale, Arizona]] and played scholastically at [[Viewmont High School]] in [[Bountiful, Utah]].<ref name="PFR1">{{Cite web |title=Kyle Morrell Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MorrKy20.htm |access-date=2025-09-21 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played [[college football|collegiately]] for the [[BYU Cougars football|BYU Cougars]],<ref name="NFL">{{cite web| url=https://www.nfl.com/players/kyle-morrell/ |title=Kyle Morrell Stats |website=NFL.com |access-date=May 28, 2024}}</ref> where, as a senior, he was a member of their [[1984 BYU Cougars football team|1984 consensus national champion team]]. He was also honored his senior year by the [[Associated Press]], as a first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]].<ref name="AP 1984">{{cite news |title=AP All-Americans |newspaper=The Indianapolis Star |date=December 5, 1984 |page=62 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/5289262/upi_and_ap_allamerica_teams/ |via=Newspapers.com}}{{open access}}</ref>

Morrell was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the fourth round of the [[1985 NFL draft]],<ref name="PFR2">{{Cite web |title=1985 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1985/draft.htm |access-date=October 10, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> but spent the year on the [[injured reserve list]].<ref name="PDH 1985.12.08">{{cite news |title=Frustration for Morrell |newspaper=Provo (UT) Daily Herald |date=December 8, 1985 |page=9 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-daily-herald-kyle-morrell-1985-injur/148251608/ |access-date=May 28, 2024 |via=Newspapers.com}}{{open access}}</ref> He appeared in five games for the Vikings in 1986.<ref name="PFA">{{Cite web |url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/playerm/morr00400.html |title=Kyle Morrell Stats |website=Pro Football Archives |access-date=May 28, 2024 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406185843/https://www.profootballarchives.com/playerm/morr00400.html |archive-date=April 6, 2023}}</ref>

Morrell died on November 15, 2020, in Bountiful, from [[Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis]] (ALS).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2020/11/17/21570297/kyle-morrell-byu-nfl-vikings-minnesota-cougars-hawaii-tom-holmoe|title=Remembering Kyle Morrell, former BYU safety and author of iconic defensive play|date=November 17, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/saltlaketribune/obituary.aspx?n=kyle-douglas-morrell&pid=197125296|title = Kyle Douglas Morrell Obituary (1963–2020) the Salt Lake Tribune| website=[[Legacy.com]] }}</ref>
